title: Aerolíneas Argentinas 322
summary: Aerolíneas Argentinas Flight 322, a de Havilland Comet, crashed during climbout from Viracopos Airport near São Paulo, Brazil at 05:38 on November 23, 1961. The aircraft was operating in dark night conditions with heavy cloud coverage that obscured visibility. After reaching approximately 100 meters altitude, the aircraft lost altitude and collided with eucalyptus trees, then crashed into the ground. All 52 aboard were killed in the impact and resulting explosions.
probable_cause: Failure to operate under IFR procedures during night takeoff in weather conditions requiring IFR operation, combined with failure to follow proper climb procedures and lack of pilot vigilance during initial climb phase.

factors.evidence: Dark night conditions removed external visual references
Broken to overcast cloud coverage with poor visibility
Failure to follow proper IFR procedures and climb procedures
Pilot lack of vigilance during climb
